---
title: "select() applies its selections in order"
ref: TDY-03
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "the columns without Species, then Species alone"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022, 2026)"
---

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

flowers <- head(iris, n = 2)
names(select(flowers, -Species, everything()))
names(select(flowers, !starts_with("Petal") | !starts_with("Sepal")))
```
:::

## Why

`select()` reads its arguments from left to right. When the first one is an exclusion, it starts from all the columns and removes `Species`, then `everything()` adds back whatever is missing, that is `Species`. The order of the arguments changes the result.

The operators follow set logic: `|` is a union. "Everything but Petal" union "everything but Sepal" contains every column, since each one escapes at least one of the two exclusions. Along the way, the columns get reordered.

## The remedy

Put the exclusion last, and write "neither one nor the other" with `&`, or by excluding a single set.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

names(select(flowers, everything(), -Species))
names(select(flowers, !starts_with("Petal") & !starts_with("Sepal")))
names(select(flowers, !c(starts_with("Petal"), starts_with("Sepal"))))
```
:::
